 is only minimally related to height and is a good predictor of visceral and total
fat mass as well as disease risk. It is relatively easily measured within the primary care and research settings, which makes it a useful
addition to the assessment of obesity by BMI. WHO guidelines specify that the circumference should be measured at the midpoint
between the lower margin of the last rib and the top of the hip bone. Waist circumference cut-points associated with increased risk
have not been fully deﬁned as yet.
